decisive_items: bone disruption of the lateral and inferior orbital walls, extension through the inferior orbital fissure, invasion of the left cavernous sinus
a discrete medial bulging of the left nasal fossa lateral wall and a leftward septal deviation
diffusion restriction around the ophthalmic nerve
response.rationale: The champion diagnosis, invasive fungal sinusitis, is supported by the patient's history of poorly controlled diabetes, aggressive bone destruction, and invasion of the orbit and sinuses. While the initial biopsy results were inconclusive, the imaging findings and laboratory results are consistent with an invasive fungal infection. The runner-up diagnosis, esthesioneuroblastoma, is also a possibility given the patient's presentation of a progressive orbital mass with extension into the sinuses and orbit, but the lack of definitive evidence of neoplasia on biopsy reduces its likelihood.

rejected.why: Biopsy results did not confirm lymphoma
No evidence of metastatic disease on biopsy
Biopsy results did not confirm squamous cell carcinoma
No evidence of granulomas on biopsy
